notes: Selectors are the ones the module actually renders today: [data-cb-home-shelf], [data-cb-home-card-action], [data-cb-block-check], [data-cb-choice], [data-cb-answer-kind], [data-cb-verdict], [data-cb-evidence-chip], [data-cb-tally-caption], [data-cb-path-current].
The submit control carries no stable data attribute, so the click falls back to the button's own label and accepts both the v2 copy and the v3 deck row (classroom.check.primary).
Run only against the accepted commit: the capture door refuses a window whose module sha is not the checkout's, and a take driven on a different module is not evidence.
A step that cannot find its target stops the take; no step is allowed to continue anyway.

Ordering rule: a shot marker fires only after the step (and its wait_for / assert) that puts the pictured state on screen. The marker log is what the editor cuts to, so a marker stamped before its state names the wrong frame.

The driven check must be the selection format: the answer step clicks [data-cb-choice="1"] and the next step asserts [data-cb-answer-kind="selection"]. A checklist or text check is refused rather than faked — a click into the textarea types nothing, and the primary stays disabled while the text is empty (desktop/plugin.js:13628), so S4a's filled primary would be unreachable.

Acts: act 1 ends at the close marker. Act 2 begins with a reconnect step that closes the take's own CDP socket and waits for a page target with a different id. In one invocation the driver announces the close and waits; with --act 1 / --act 2 the window is closed and reopened between the two runs. Act 2 can never stamp the resume frame on the page act 1 was attached to.
